items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Benny Carter took the microphone and says, “Bob if you don’t mind I’d like to hear a little Dick Katz in that place.”

ctx.x: Oh, the story that goes with that date. It was very relaxed and I remember Coleman, I think he might have been wearing a tux because he was working in the Metropole or

something. It was very nice. We did it in two days, a lot of musicians there, and Benny Carter’s music plays itself. But now this is a class man, this Benny Carter. Because listen to what he did. On one of the tunes I had the bridge to play a little solo. Just eight bars I think. And I played it. I don’t remember which tune, it was probably “Honeysuckle Rose.” So when I did it Bob Thiele from the control room, after we did the take he says, “Uh Dick, can we have a little Count Basie in that spot?” Benny Carter…

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: with Jimmy Garrison on base and Dick Katz on piano, and Joe Jones on drums and John Collins on guitar

ctx.x: Field, mentioned to me -- he'd like me to, you know, just use the saxophone section and recreate a couple of things that Coleman Hawkins and I had done in Paris many years earlier with the two French saxophone players, Andre Ekyan, the altoist, and Alex Combelle, who is a tenor saxophone player; so we got together, oh, Phil Woods on the other alto and Charlie Rouse on the other tenor, Coleman Hawkins, myself -- with Jimmy Garrison on base and Dick Katz on piano, and Joe Jones on drums and John Collins on guitar,…
And you did a few of the tunes of those famous brase.
